records.name: Malta
records.summary_text:
Malta is among the safest countries in the world for transgender visitors. It has ranked first for LGBTI legal rights in its region every year since 2015: gender identity and expression are protected from discrimination in law, legal gender recognition works by self-determination, and 'X' gender markers are available on passports. Conversion therapy is banned and the constitution guarantees LGBTI equality.

records.name: Iceland
records.summary_text:
Iceland ranks first of 121 regions surveyed by Equaldex as a good place for gay and lesbian people, with a 93 per cent rating. Same-sex sexual activity is legal for men and women, same-sex marriage is recognised in law, and gender change carries no restrictions. Legal gender recognition operates through a self-determination process introduced by the 2019 reform that replaced the country's earlier, already progressive framework, and non-binary identity is recognised in law.

records.name: Spain
records.summary_text:
Ley 4/2023, published on 28 February 2023, grants legal gender recognition on self-identification. Under Article 43 any person aged 16 or over may request rectification of the gender mention on their own registry entry before the Civil Registry, without the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment.
